name: Typed exec protocol: agent loop requests, client executes
what: The agent loop runs on the server (or in the cloud Box) and asks a user-owned computer to perform tool calls; results and streamed output come back as typed messages. The same protocol carries cancel, heartbeat and error frames.
how: protobuf ExecServerMessage with an id, exec_id and optional machine_id routes one of about 37 argument kinds (shell and shell_stream, background_shell_spawn, write_shell_stdin, read/redacted_read, write, delete, ls, grep, diagnostics, request_context, mcp plus resource and state calls, fetch, record_screen, computer_use, execute_hook, subagent plus await and force_background, smart_mode_classifier, canvas_diagnostics, three allowlist prechecks, git_diff, pi_* and mini_swe_agent_bash shims, conversation_search, agent_store_conflict) with a W3C span_context. ExecClientMessage mirrors every case as a result and adds local_execution_time_ms and hook_additional_contexts; ExecClientControlMessage has stream_close, throw and heartbeat; ExecServerControlMessage has abort.
verevonRelevance: Gives Verevon a concrete template for a typed, cancellable, traceable tool-exec channel between the Model Plane agent loop and a user-owned computer (the "agent PC" case), beyond the current credential-free sandbox lease.
notes: Cursor-platform heritage (agent.v1 package) rather than Grok-specific invention. Quality 5 because every call is typed, traced, cancellable and machine-addressable.

name: Pluggable executor registry with cancellable streaming handlers
what: Each tool kind is handled by a registered executor; long-running tools stream events and can be aborted mid-flight without leaving state behind.
how: The daemon builds an ExecManager (oYe) that registers typed handlers for shell, write, read and ls on top of shared policy stubs; handleExecRequest creates a per-request cancel context, iterates the manager as an async generator, converts results to JSON frames and maps a thrown error to a control throw frame that also reports whether the working directory still exists. handleCancel flips a flag and sends an abort control message with the stored exec id. An executor registry keyed by DI tokens (computerUseExecutor, fetchExecutor, diagnosticsExecutor and similar) registers argument and result case names per tool.
verevonRelevance: Pattern for adding executors (browser, shell, file) behind one cancellable stream interface in the Model Plane runtime.
notes: Common engineering pattern; included because cancellation and cwd-state reporting are done carefully. Quality calibrated to 3: solid but a feature peers commonly ship.

name: Large model-facing tool catalogue (117 named tools)
what: The agent sees one flat set of tools that cover the computer (Shell, Read, Computer, Screenshot, AwaitShell), teammates and channels (SendMessage, SendToUser, SendToAgent, ReactToMessage, CreateChannel), work (CreateTask, ReadTask, UpdateTask, Subagent tools), documents and canvases, email, calendar and meetings, credentials, MCP and plugin management, memory, skills, billing checks and even app-home and avatar updates.
how: A single tool-name enum (Bt) shared across daemon and host code, e.g. AddMcpServer, AwaitShell, BrowserSecureFill, CopyToBox, CopyFromBox, FillCredential, JoinMeeting, ListMachines, RecallMemory, RequestVirtualCard, SetPrimaryBot, UpdateRoutine, WakeParent, WebFetch, WebSearch, WriteDocument. The enum is used to compose model-facing approval and refusal text, so tool names are a stable contract.
verevonRelevance: Shows the breadth of "agent as teammate" tools (task, channel, meeting, credential, plugin self-management) a Space agent would need; useful checklist for the Verevon agent tool registry.
notes: Counts come from the enum literal; not every tool is necessarily exposed to every agent (plan and harness gating unknown).

name: Two agent harnesses: per-user Box vs server-hosted durable (Temporal)
what: Agents can live in the user's own cloud computer (box) or be hosted by the server as durable agents (temporal). Group chats, agent messaging and server rooms exist only for the server-hosted kind; the client asks the server which route to use.
how: Coordinator createAgent and createGroup take a creationRoute of {kind:"box"} or {kind:"temporal", scope}. resolveAgentCreation asks the server; a box route is dispatched through the local host, a temporal route through a server RPC and fails with failureCode temporal-creation-refused when unsupported ("Server-hosted rooms are not supported by this server"; group chats need a team account that can create server-hosted bots). GrokBotRuntimeCapabilities exposes durable_identity_enabled, durable_identity_writes_enabled, temporal_creation_enabled, agent_messaging_enabled, server_rooms_enabled; a harness-migration rollout status adds migration_gate_enabled, identity_reads_enabled, temporal_harness_mode, room_promotion_enabled and empty_flip_enabled. Credential decisions are tagged with a harness of BOX or TEMPORAL.
verevonRelevance: Strong evidence that a leading agent product is moving from "agent lives inside a per-user VM" to "durable server-side run plus on-demand computer", which matches the Model Plane session/run design and should be copied (sandbox as a tool, not as the agent home).
notes: Naming suggests Temporal.io durable workflows but no Temporal SDK is shipped in the client; that mapping is INF (basis: terms durable identity, temporal harness, server rooms). Medium confidence on exact semantics.

name: Per-user cloud computer ("Box") lifecycle
what: Every bot owner has a persistent cloud computer that can be absent, hibernated, starting or running, can be upgraded on a schedule, migrated between hosts, snapshotted and wiped, and is shown to the user as a desktop.
how: Enums: SandBoxRunState (ABSENT, HIBERNATED, RUNNING, STARTING), SandBoxUpgradeScheduleState (SCHEDULED, CLAIMED, RUNNING, WAITING_FOR_IMAGE, COMPLETED, MISSED, FAILED, CANCELLED), SandBoxMigrationPhase (BACKING_UP, CREATING, MOVING, CLEANING_UP, WIPING, DONE, FAILED). EnsureSandBox takes wake and supports_asleep_box; GetSandBoxRunState returns state, image_update_available and egress_tunnel_ownership. The coordinator maps box failures to box-blocked (with a user-facing title and detail), no-storage and access-denied. Admin RPCs hibernate, snapshot, restore, update host and bulk kill, recreate or delete boxes for team members.
verevonRelevance: Defines the lifecycle surface Verevon would need if each Space agent gets a persistent PC: hibernate/wake, image upgrades, migration, snapshots and user-visible blocked states.
notes: Server side not visible; only client descriptors and enums.

name: Presence-aware parking of the Box connection (away-park, present-park, client-pause)
what: When the user is away or the work does not need the computer, the desktop stops holding the Box open so it can sleep, and wakes it only on user intent; an emergency pause can stop all Box access from a client.
how: Feature gates sand_client_pause, sand_desktop_away_park, sand_desktop_present_park and sand_desktop_park_retires_local_exec drive setGatewayPaused({paused, reason client-pause|away-park|present-park, nobodyPresent, presentPark, parkRetiresLocalExec}). A pure decision function returns wake, hold or follow from backend keep-asleep, presence (away), whether the computer window is open, a roster census (all-temporal) and an intentUntilMs deadline. Away is judged from system idle seconds with a ten-minute scale; a pause rejects connect, recreate and credential-issue calls with SandClientPausedError.
verevonRelevance: Directly applicable cost control for Verevon agent PCs: tie sandbox keep-alive to human presence and explicit intent, with a remote kill-switch gate; ties into cost per Space.
notes: No peer in the reference set (Teams, Slack, buzz, qm) is known to have this; best-in-class resource discipline for always-on agent computers (INF on peers: not verified here).

name: Intent-classified calls so background work never wakes a sleeping computer
what: Calls the user did not trigger (status polling, secret presence checks, attachment reads) are tagged so they do not wake the Box, while user actions do.
how: A table maps every coordinator method to a class: person (createAgentAutomation, handBackForeverBox, startTeachRecording, uploadAttachment, injectChromeCookies and others), background (getHostStatus, setBoxSecrets, refreshMcp, listBoxMcpServers, setWindowFocused, gateway, passkey-provider, cookie-provider) or describes (local-exec-refresh). Attachment reads have an IfAwake variant, and a mayViewerWakeBox predicate gates VNC header injection.
evidence: REA inspect_analysis_view(modules item dist/node-agent-coordinator/main.cjs) static_analysis: requires node:http/https/http2, node:dns/promises, node:child_process, node:crypto, node:zlib; endpoint-like tokens local-exec-refresh, gateway, passkey-provider, cookie-provider
verevonRelevance: Adopt a "person vs background" intent tag on every Space-plane call that touches an agent sandbox to avoid billing wake-ups from polling.
notes: Pairs with away-park; the mapping is hand-maintained.

name: User computer as a second machine for the agent (machineId routing)
what: The agent can run shell, read and file-transfer tools either on its own Box or on a registered machine of the user (desktop, phone); one machine is chosen per call, and ambiguity is refused.
how: Machines are registered with label, kind, local_tool_permission, messages_enabled and heartbeat (SandMachine, RegisterSandMachine). Tools accept machineId; the default machine id is "this-computer". If more than one user machine is registered the call is refused with a message telling the model to call ListMachines and retry with machineId. CopyToBox and CopyFromBox move files between machines. Phone machines advertise mobile_local_tools.
verevonRelevance: Model for "agents with own PC plus access to the human's PC": explicit machine registry, per-machine permission and refusal of ambiguous routing.
notes: Cross-room rule: a bot on the user machine cannot share a room with a teammate bot (scout inventory, SRC strings).

name: Local-tool permission model: never, ask, always with team ceiling
what: The user sets whether bots may act on their computer (Never, Ask, Always), can override it per machine, and a team policy can cap it; denials are remembered for the task.
how: Levels never<ask<always (xA returns the lower of setting and ceiling). Settings localToolPermission, localToolPermissionCeiling and localToolPermissionByMachineId are stored per account scope. Nine local-use actions are classified: run-command, send-input, read-file, list-directory, write-file and read-ai-tool-setup are global; read-messages is setting-gated; send-imessage is subject-scoped (per recipient); run-phone-tool is call-scoped. fQ returns allow, ask or refused using the setting, ceiling, an approvals file with a retirement file, and (for server-authoritative connections) the server-issued authorization instead of the local setting.
verevonRelevance: Concrete model for Verevon browser/PC grants: ordered levels, org ceiling, per-machine override, per-subject standing grants and server-authoritative decisions (compatible with Control-signed decisions).
notes: Quality 5 for the layering (user setting, org ceiling, per-action approval, standing grants, server authority).

name: Standing grants scoped to action or recipient
what: After approving a sensitive action the user can allow it again for the same action or only for the same recipient, without being asked each time.
how: A standing-grants file keyed by [accountScope, scope, action(, recipient)] stores grantedAtMs; recipients are trimmed, single-line and limited to 320 characters; only subject-scoped actions (send-imessage) are eligible, only when the setting is not Never and no explicit approval id is present. Approvals are per approvalId and are matched against action plus target (or the terminals resource path for command attachment), then retired in a retirement list so a replayed approval cannot run twice.
verevonRelevance: Fits Verevon approval grants: scope grants to (action, subject) and retire one-shot approvals to prevent replay (current Space approvals are not resumed).
notes: Only implemented for messaging subjects in this build.

name: Approval and refusal copy written for the model
what: When the user declines, is unreachable or settings forbid the action, the tool returns instructions that tell the model not to retry, to use its own computer, or to ask the user, and says when the decision is remembered.
how: Constants in the daemon cover: local tools off (do not retry while the setting stays Never), user declined (do not retry; do something else or ask), already asked and not approved this task (a later permission change does not authorize it), earlier requests unanswered and user moved on, request too long to show for approval (split it or use the own computer), Messages off. Texts reference tool names through the Bt enum.
verevonRelevance: Verevon approval denials should return machine-actionable guidance to the agent (do not retry, fallback path) rather than a bare error.
notes: Texts are model instructions, not user UI; paraphrased here.

name: Auto-review: natural-language allow and block rules plus a risk classifier
what: Instead of approving each action, users keep a short list of plain-language rules (for example allow emails to specific people); a classifier decides allow, ask or block using the rules and the conversation, and the UI suggests rules from recipient lists.
how: autoReviewInstructions {isEnabled, allowInstructions[], blockInstructions[]} with at most 20 rules of 1000 characters each, deduplicated and trimmed; a rule helper builds "Emails to a, b or c" text from recipients and can replace an existing rule. The exec protocol has SmartModeClassifierArgs (risk target with action and arguments plus conversation_context) returning a success or error result. Approval modes in the UI are always-allow, needs-approval and disable-drafts.
verevonRelevance: Reduces approval fatigue for Verevon: an org/user policy in natural language evaluated by a model, with deterministic fallbacks, sits well beside Control decisions.
notes: Classifier prompts and models are server-side; only the interface is visible.

name: Per-scope tool permission matrix and MCP tool controls
what: Users and teams can set each tool or connector scope to always allow, needs approval or blocked, with separate defaults for reads and writes, disable individual MCP tools, and add custom instructions per MCP server.
how: Settings schema toolPermissions {scopes: {name: {tools: {tool: always_allow|needs_approval|blocked}, reads, writes}}}, mcpDisabledToolsByServerId, mcpCustomInstructions and mcpCustomInstructionsByServerId; connector always-allow state can be cleared (ClearGrokBotConnectorAlwaysAllow, ResolveGrokBotConnectorGrant).
verevonRelevance: Matches the allowed_tools and approval_mode fields on Verevon agent bindings; the reads/writes defaults per scope are a neat refinement.
notes: Teams and Slack have app permission scopes; this applies them to tool-level agent permissions. Quality calibrated to 3: solid but a feature peers commonly ship.

name: Shell tool runtime: shell flavours, working-directory fallback and process-tree kill
what: Commands run in the right shell for the OS, fall back to a safe root if the requested directory is missing (and tell the model), and are killed as a whole tree on cancel.
how: Shell enum zsh, zsh-light, bash, powershell, naive; default env TERM=dumb, NO_COLOR=1, FORCE_COLOR=0. A missing workingDirectory is replaced by the local-exec root and a stderr line explains it. Kill strategy is chosen by platform and spawn mode (windows_tree, process_group or single_process).
verevonRelevance: Baseline behaviours for any Verevon shell tool (cwd fallback message to the model, tree kill on cancel).
notes: Quality calibrated to 3: solid but a feature peers commonly ship.

name: Background shells with durable terminal files and await/stdin tools
what: Long-running commands move to the background; their live output is written to a text file the agent can read later, and the agent can wait for them, write to stdin, or push a foreground command to the background.
how: Each shell gets terminals/<shellId>.txt with a front-matter header (pid, cwd, command, title, status, started_at, running_for_ms refreshed every 5 s), the streamed stdout and stderr, optional [stdin] echoes, and a footer with exit_code, elapsed_ms and ended_at. Exec kinds background_shell_spawn, force_background_shell, write_shell_stdin and the AwaitShell tool operate on it; existing running shells can be adopted by a new turn through an event iterator.
verevonRelevance: The file-per-process transcript with header and footer is a durable, model-readable contract worth copying for the Verevon background process registry (sandbox-manager).
notes: Verevon already has a background process registry (read side); this adds output-as-file and await semantics.

name: Pattern-triggered wake-ups from background shell output
what: The agent can ask to be notified when a running command prints something matching a pattern (for example a build finishing), instead of polling.
how: An output observer watches stdout and stderr of a shell against a regular expression, batches matches with a flush timer, and enqueues task_progress items (title, detail with occurrence numbers, outputPath) into a backgroundWorkRegistry keyed by conversation; a notification limit emits a final "limit reached" item and tells the model to read the file directly. Invalid patterns are logged and ignored.
verevonRelevance: Event-driven agent wake-up from process output fits Space watches (S4.3) and removes polling for long sandbox jobs.

name: Computer use on the user's own desktop through a native sidecar (macOS only here)
what: The agent can see the screen and click, type, scroll, drag and press keys on the user's Mac in batches, with the user in control of when input is active; there is no Windows implementation in this build.
how: The daemon talks newline-delimited JSON over a unix socket to a sidecar app ("Cursor Computer Use", executable CUCursorService) located through service.json; methods ping, control/start, control/release and tools/call with names computer_use_screenshot, _click, _mouse_move, _mouse_button, _drag, _scroll, _typing, _press_key and _check_permissions; 45 s call timeout, 8 s launch wait, relaunch-and-retry on ENOENT or ECONNREFUSED, response size cap. An action executor runs a batch (screenshot, click, scroll, mouseMove, mouseDown, mouseUp, drag, type, key, wait, cursorPosition), starts a control session only if the batch has input actions and always releases it, then returns actionCount, durationMs, screenshot and cursor position. Screenshots are re-encoded to lossless WebP with a wasm codec; held keys are rejected.
evidence: REA inspect_analysis_view(modules item dist/local-exec-daemon/main.cjs) static_analysis: requires node:child_process x14, node:net x3, node:http/https/http2/tls, node:sqlite, worker_threads, tree-sitter, tree-sitter-bash; 244 route-like endpoint literals (sandbox read-path list)
verevonRelevance: Windows desktop computer use is absent here, so Verevon cannot copy a Windows path; the control-session and batch-action design is reusable (acquire control only for input actions, always release).
notes: The scout inventory listed computer_use tools as local; this run shows the local-desktop path is mac-sidecar backed. A Linux X11 driver exists (see the Box record); no Windows driver or code path was found (INF, medium) in this 0.70.2 Windows build.

name: Remote-desktop computer use on the Box (X11 driver, desktop lease, settle time)
what: Inside the Box the agent drives a Linux desktop with the same action vocabulary, with optional typing delay and a wait before the screenshot so pages can settle.
how: ComputerUseArgs carries tool_call_id, actions[], description, bind_unmapped_characters, desktop_lease_actor_id, screenshot_settle_ms and native_x11_driver {typing_delay_ms, allow_fallback}. The daemon bundle also contains the Linux executor: drivers native_x11 or xdotool, display size read with xrandr (including refresh rate), a scaler that maps a model-facing frame (default 1280 px wide, 1920x1200 display) to real pixels and back with an aspect-ratio guard (0.02 tolerance, otherwise an error), mouse button and scroll mappings, cursor-type detection through xdotool and xprop, and an action recorder that stores timestamp, command duration, position before and after and cursor type for each action. Metrics computer_use.session.duration_ms, .action_count, .result, .action_kind and computer_use.desktop_lease.check (outcome, reason) are emitted. A desktop lease actor id suggests exclusive control of the shared desktop between the human viewer and the agent (INF).
verevonRelevance: Same action schema can drive a Linux sandbox desktop behind Quarry-style grants; lease actor id is a clean way to arbitrate human vs agent input.
notes: Corrects the first draft: the Linux X11 executor IS shipped in the daemon bundle (the same daemon runs inside the Box). Semantics of desktop_lease_actor_id are INF; the lease check implementation was not located.

name: Screen recording tool and teach-by-demonstration messages
what: The user can record a task on screen to teach the bot; the recording is saved and sent as a message so the bot can learn the procedure.
how: RecordScreenArgs {mode, tool_call_id, save_as_filename} returns start_success (with wasPriorRecordingCancelled), save_success, discard_success or failure; the coordinator exposes start/stopTeachRecording({agentId, entryPoint, save}) and getTeachRecordingStatus; a user-message initiator TEACH_RECORDING marks the resulting message.
verevonRelevance: A demonstration-to-skill capture path is a differentiator for agent onboarding; no equivalent in Verevon today.
notes: How the recording becomes a skill is server side.

name: Live desktop view of the Box via an embedded noVNC page
what: The user can watch (and optionally take over) the bot's computer inside the app; the view pauses when hidden and reports connect, reconnect and disconnect.
how: The Box serves the stock noVNC page (/vnc.html) into an Electron webview on a dedicated session partition; a webview preload observes noVNC state classes (noVNC_connected, reconnecting, connecting, disconnecting) and sends sand:vnc-session phases (rfb_connect, reconnect, rfb_disconnect), forwards arrow keys to the host, and holds rendering when the view is hidden. Main injects per-host auth headers from URL tokens into requests, locks zoom, routes host shortcuts via before-input-event and bridges the clipboard through a trust-checked IPC transport.
verevonRelevance: Pragmatic path for human viewing of an agent PC: reuse noVNC inside a locked-down webview with token-to-header injection, instead of a custom remote-desktop stack.
notes: Verevon baseline has RustDesk-based remote support (browser to hbbs/hbbr); noVNC is simpler for sandbox desktops.

name: Egress tunnel: the Box exits to the internet through the user's own computer
what: The user can let the bot's cloud computer route network traffic via their desktop (for example to reach allow-listed or intranet resources), with one computer holding the tunnel at a time.
how: The desktop attaches a WebSocket (ws) tunnel client with a bearer token to an egress endpoint in claim or if-free mode, with an attach-generation header so the same computer can reclaim its slot; it takes ownership ("another computer holds the tunnel; standing by"), multiplexes TCP streams over binary frames after name resolution, uses ping and pong as a liveness watchdog, refuses streams blocked by network policy, monitors Box liveness and reconnects. A policy loop refetches the account network policy with 5-attempt backoff (2 s to 30 s); loosening refreshes are applied only for their tightening half ("reconnect the box to loosen"); after repeated failures the cached policy is dropped and the tunnel detaches. Settings egressTunnelEnabled (default off) and localEgressAllowed gate it.
verevonRelevance: Useful for enterprise customers whose systems accept only company IPs: agent PC egress via the customer's machine, with fail-closed, tighten-only policy updates.
notes: Scout inventory only saw policy strings; this run read the client.

name: Chrome login portability: import real cookies into the bot's browser with per-origin approval
what: The user can lend their signed-in Chrome sessions to the bot's browser for chosen sites; the app asks per origin before any cookie is copied. Unavailable on Windows in this build.
how: A worker copies Chrome's Cookies SQLite (plus -wal and -shm; on macOS falls back to a Finder AppleScript duplicate when the copy is denied), reads rows through node:sqlite, derives the AES key from the "Chrome Safe Storage" secret with PBKDF2 and decrypts v10 and v11 values, strips the host-hash prefix and converts expiry, SameSite and priority. The coordinator asks main to present a per-origin approval (origins with profile ids) and to remember list-access grants, then injectChromeCookies sends the approved cookies to the Box. Platform gate allows only darwin and linux.
verevonRelevance: Browser-grant design for Quarry: explicit per-origin consent plus cookie injection into the agent browser; note the Windows gap (DPAPI/app-bound encryption) when planning a Windows desktop agent.
notes: Not executed. Security trade-off: raw session cookies leave the user device; approval is the only control.

name: WebAuthn/passkey proxy to the user's security key
what: When a site in the bot's remote browser asks for a passkey, the request is forwarded to the user's desktop, which asks consent (origin and relying party), prompts for a PIN if needed, signs with the local authenticator and returns the assertion.
how: A reverse WebAuthn channel (coordinator providers webauthn-connect, -heartbeat, -stall, -delivery, -denial-mute and webauthn-reconnect) calls main for consent and PIN prompts, then spawns the native helper sand-webauthn-signer(.exe) with JSON on stdin; the helper reports pin-required and pin-invalid events on stderr and the final result on stdout; a windowHandle parents native UI. The setting webauthnProxyEnabled defaults to true. The same helper backs passkey-based spend approvals.
verevonRelevance: A human-in-the-loop answer for agent browsers that must authenticate with passkeys, keeping the private key on the user device.
notes: Helper binary not analysed (REA lists it with no PE resources).

name: Secrets and credentials for agents: vault with domain-bound rules and lifecycle
what: Bots get secrets from the user or team, never shown to teammates, injected into forms or requests only for matching sites; credentials can expire, enter a grace period or be rejected by the provider.
how: Box secrets are set by the host (setBoxSecrets, getBoxSecretsStatus, carryBoxSecretsToBot; combined size limit enforced). Vault credentials carry target rules (EXACT_HOST_PORT or REGISTRABLE_DOMAIN), a lifecycle state (ACTIVE, EXPIRING, GRACE, EXPIRED, PROVIDER_REJECTED) and an expiration mode (DISABLED, WARN, ENFORCE). Tools FillCredential, BrowserSecureFill, ListCredentials, ListAvailableSecureValues and RequestUserForm let the agent request values without seeing them.
verevonRelevance: Domain-bound credential injection (host/registrable-domain rules) plus expiry modes is a concrete schema for Verevon browser grants and secret handling.
notes: Secrets never read; only schema names.

name: 1Password-backed secrets (service account or OAuth broker)
what: Users can connect 1Password so bots draw credentials from vaults; connections sync manually or when the app gains focus and credential requests require approval.
how: OnePasswordConnectionKind SERVICE_ACCOUNT or OAUTH_BROKER, broker state PAIRING, CONNECTED or RECONNECT_REQUIRED, sync trigger MANUAL or APP_FOCUS; a dedicated service process (onepassword-connection-service.cjs) and coordinator check isOnePasswordAppInstalled; RPCs approve or deny a credential request.
verevonRelevance: Optional enterprise integration; shows the broker pattern (agent asks, human approves, secret never shown).

name: Agent spending with virtual cards and passkey-approved spend
what: A bot can request a virtual card for a purchase; the user approves with a passkey before money can move.
how: RaiseGrokBotVirtualCard {amount_cents, currency, merchant_name, merchant_url, context}; BeginGrokBotSpendApproval {request_id, payment_method_id, mode, enrollment_ticket}; coordinator methods resolveVirtualCardApproval, beginSpendApproval, listVirtualCardPaymentMethods; tool RequestVirtualCard.
verevonRelevance: Hard-limit pattern for agent purchases: per-request amount and merchant bound approvals with strong authentication; would plug into Control decisions and cost-core.
notes: Payment rails are server side.

name: Subagents with continuation policy and per-subagent credentials
what: A bot can start, message, await, interrupt and stop subagents (read-only or full, in the background), and the parent is woken when children finish.
how: SubagentArgs: subagent_type, model_id, prompt, readonly, resume_agent_id, run_in_background, parent_conversation_id and root_parent_conversation_id, fork_agent_id, mode, selected_context, environment, cloud_base_branch, model_parameters, BYOK credentials (API key, Azure or Bedrock), and a continuation config (idleThreshold, maxLoops, nudgeMessage, escapeMessageTemplate, collectBackgroundChildren, childrenCompletedMessageTemplate, continuationRoundDelayMs). Tools CheckSubagent, MessageSubagent, StopSubagent, WakeParent; subagent sessions are named with the sand-subagent- prefix and task:<id>[:parent] keys.
verevonRelevance: The continuation config (nudge, loop cap, collect children) is a ready design for Verevon subagent results, which currently carry no Space context.

name: Server-orchestrated multi-agent rooms (turn requests with nonce, deadline, wind-down)
what: In group chats several bots take turns; each bot can answer, stay silent, or work and report later, and the room can wind down.
how: RequestGrokBotRoomMemberTurn {nonce, room, member_agent_id, peers[], new_messages[], is_winding_down, deadline_ms, parent_request_id, root_parent_request_id} and DeliverGrokBotRoomMemberTurnResult {room_id, nonce, outcome, messages, error, posts[]}. Coordinator result kinds include work_landed, work_overheard, user_message and tool stay_silent. Group usage costs more because every member processes each message (scout string).
verevonRelevance: Loop-safe multi-agent room protocol (nonce idempotency, deadline, parent and root request ids) is the missing piece for Verevon agent-to-agent delegation in a Space.
notes: Which agent speaks next is decided server side.

name: Direct agent-to-agent messaging
what: One bot can message another bot directly, outside a human room, when the server enables agent messaging.
how: SendGrokBotAgentMessage {from_agent_id, to_agent_id, message_id, text, sent_at_ms, reply_to_id}; tool SendToAgent; runtime flag agent_messaging_enabled.
verevonRelevance: Agent-to-agent delegation is absent in Verevon Spaces; a minimal message RPC with idempotent ids is the starting point.

name: Memory, recall and context handoff tools
what: Bots keep memories per user and team, can recall past conversations (including phone calls), sort and promote memories to a team, and read the main bot's context.
how: Tools UpdateMemory, RecallMemory, SortMemories, SetUserAttribute, UpdateState, ReadTranscript, ReadAgentActivity; exec kind conversation_search lets the server search client-held transcripts; coordinator readMainAgentContext and getConversationOutline; carry-over steps list plugins, skills, memories and files; PromoteGrokBotMemoriesToTeam. The voice agent has recall_text_messages and search_conversations tools with scope this-chat, earlier or everything.
verevonRelevance: Memory scopes per person, bot and team (not per room) are visible; Verevon lacks a Space memory scope.
notes: Memory storage and ranking are server side; client exposes the plumbing only.

name: Habit mining: a prompt that studies transcripts and writes an index for all future agents
what: A background analysis pass reads stored conversation transcripts to find repeated user behaviours and writes a concise index file shown to agents later.
how: A packaged prompt tells the analyser where transcripts live (agentTranscriptsPath, human-readable .txt files), what to look for (repeated behaviours) and to produce a compact index.md for future agents.
verevonRelevance: Cheap way to turn transcript history into agent-visible preferences; needs ZDR-aware handling in Verevon.
notes: Trigger and schedule not found; may be an internal experiment.

name: Scheduled routines and automations with machine-readable failure hints
what: Users define named automations (prompt plus trigger), toggle them, run them now, and get structured reasons when a run cannot start (plan, limits, repo access, client update needed).

Failures return an x-automation-failure-hint header from a closed list (CONCURRENT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, CLOUD_AGENT_PLAN_RESTRICTED, SAND_BOX_BLOCKED, SAND_CLIENT_UPDATE_REQUIRED, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE and about 30 more).

name: Draft-first external messaging with a per-bot switch
what: Bots can draft outbound messages (email, calendar invites, external chat) for the user to review and send, and the user can turn drafting off or always allow specific recipients.

name: Harness compatibility shims for external coding agents (pi, mini-SWE-agent)

name: Lifecycle hooks executed on the client: ten wire events, 21 hook names and a Claude-compatible name map
what: Users and teams can attach scripts that run before and after tool calls, on prompt submit, on stop, on sub-agent start and stop and before context compaction; a hook can allow, deny or ask, rewrite tool input, inject context or ask the agent to continue.

Queries carry conversation_id, generation_id, model and model params; PreToolUse adds tool_name, tool_input, tool_use_id, cwd and parent_tool_call_id and its response may return permission (allow, deny, ask), user_message, agent_message, updated_input and additional_context; BeforeSubmitPrompt can return continue=false; Stop and SubagentStop can return a followup_message that re-enters the loop; PostToolUseFailure reports failure_type and is_interrupt; PreCompact reports context usage percent and tokens. The client event enum has 21 names (including beforeShellExecution, beforeMCPExecution, beforeReadFile, afterFileEdit, sessionStart, sessionEnd, workspaceOpen) and a map from Claude Code hook names (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SubagentStop, SessionStart, SessionEnd, PreCompact; PermissionRequest and Notification unmapped). Shell calls can carry a hook approval requirement, and HooksConfigInfo.configured_steps tells the server which steps exist. accept_hook_additional_contexts is a flag on the exec message.

name: Dedicated computer-use model and parameters per account
what: Users or teams can choose which model drives computer use, including max mode and model parameters, separately from the chat model.
how: Settings computerUseModel {modelId, maxMode, parameters[{id, value}]} validated with a non-empty modelId; GetGrokBotUserRuntimeSettings and UpdateGrokBotUserRuntimeSettings; GetGrokBotRuntimeCapabilities.
verevonRelevance: Browser/computer-use calls are vision-heavy; a separate model slot lets Verevon route them to the cheapest capable model.

name: Cloud agents and background workers as a tool
what: A bot can launch cloud coding agents against repositories and branches, with plan and policy failures reported back.

verevonRelevance: Delegating code work to a separate sandbox run is already a Model Plane capability; failure-hint vocabulary is reusable.
notes: Inherited from the Cursor cloud-agent platform.

name: SSE reverse channel: the cloud calls into the user's computer without inbound ports
what: The desktop keeps one outbound connection open and the server pushes tool requests down it; the computer answers by posting results back, so nothing needs to listen on the user machine.
how: GET /local-exec/requests with Accept text/event-stream; frames are SSE "data:" JSON blocks (blank-line delimited, oversize frames rejected with a file-error for the request id). On connect the daemon posts a hello frame (localRoot, terminalsFolder, computerId, label, supervised, variant, capabilities {messagesOp, generation}); the server answers welcome with a providerId. Responses go to POST /local-exec/responses as {providerId, frames[]} through an outbox that flushes in batches. Timers: connect deadline 15 s, stall watchdog 35 s without bytes, heartbeat ping every 10 s (also re-checks that the connection record has not moved), post deadlines 10 s control and 120 s data, 3 post attempts at 200 ms, reconnect backoff 1 s to 10 s, forced re-resolve of the connection after 3 consecutive failures. Request kinds: exec, download, upload, discover-ai-tool, cancel, retire-approval, messages-op.

name: One daemon, many connections: Box gateway plus per-account server channels
what: A single local daemon serves the Box over its gateway and, in parallel, one server-authoritative channel per signed-in account, so several accounts can use the same computer safely.
how: The daemon main loop creates one SSE provider for the Box and, for every account scope in an encrypted connection record, a separate server provider (mj) with its own executor, machine id and credential; descriptors are rebuilt when a record changes. Server-authoritative accounts skip the local permission setting because the server already attached an authorization (approval or standing). A rejected account scope is remembered and published in the discovery record so the supervisor can mint a fresh credential. Server RPCs: WatchGrokBotUserComputerRequests, OpenGrokBotUserComputerRequest, PollGrokBotUserComputerRequests, SubmitGrokBotUserComputerResponses, IssueGrokBotUserComputerCredential (credential with expires_at_ms and server_authoritative). The Box-side credential is fetched from the Box gateway path /sand-box/local-exec-daemon-credential.
verevonRelevance: Multi-tenant local runner design: scope every channel, executor and approval by account so a shared PC never mixes principals.
notes: Polling variant exists as a fallback to the streaming RPC.

name: Resumable transcript tail with per-agent cursors and generations
what: The chat list and open transcripts stay live and recover cleanly after disconnects, device sleep or server-side resets, without refetching everything.
how: WatchGrokBotTranscripts (server stream) takes cursors [{agentId, generation, afterUpdatedSeq, sessionId}], include_unlisted_agents and inline_body_max_bytes. Frames: rows (entries and deletes with seq and updatedSeq), cleared (new generation), cursorTooOld (forces a rehydrate), agentState, computerActions, agentStateChanged, rosterChanged, turnFailed, boxState, pageTitleChanged, connected, heartbeat. Row bodies are fetched separately by seq (pendingBodies) and cached in a bounded LRU of per-agent states with eviction of settled states and an epoch bump. A rehydrate emits a snapshot with coverage {kind: transcript-live-range, fromSequence, throughSequence}. Modes shadow-compare, store-first and server-tail let the client migrate between the legacy store and the server tail with parity and row-loss telemetry.
verevonRelevance: Replaces Verevon 6 s polling with a cursor-based push tail; the generation plus updatedSeq plus cursorTooOld triple is a robust resync contract.
notes: Quality 5: explicit generations, bounded memory, migration-safe modes and parity telemetry.

name: Idempotent send pipeline with journal, nonce and echo confirmation
what: Messages typed while offline or during a restart are never lost or sent twice; the composer shows queued, sending and accepted states and surfaces clear error codes.
how: Stages queued, prepared, dispatching, accepted-awaiting-echo; resolutions dispatched, retired, parked, failed; ack results acked, failed, timeout, queued_offline. A persisted send-journal (and composer-drafts) records each send; SendGrokBotUserMessage carries message_id, sent_at_ms, session_id, machine_id, traceparent, enter and compose timestamps, source, initiator and send_source; GetGrokBotSendStatus returns pending, accepted (with echo_entry_id and accepted_at_ms), rejected (rejection_code) or not-found. Client errors SAND-E0703 nonceMismatch, E0704 capabilityUnavailable, E0705 hostRejected, E0706 superseded, E0707 ackExpired.
verevonRelevance: Gold standard for exactly-once-ish chat send; Verevon Space composer has no journal, status or echo confirmation today.
notes: Echo confirmation means the client waits for the server transcript row, not just an HTTP 200.

name: UI talks to a dedicated coordinator process over a MessagePort
what: Chat state, sending and background reconnects live outside the UI renderer, so the UI stays responsive and survives renderer reloads.
how: Main forks a utility process (serviceName for the node agent coordinator, NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1, system proxy env) and, when a renderer asks, creates a MessageChannelMain and sends one port with sand:coordinator-port; the preload exposes coordinatorPort and delivers it to the renderer. REA reports 2 utility processes, 4 browser windows, 6 context-bridge APIs and 13 of 15 IPC operations with dynamic channels, consistent with this design.

verevonRelevance: For a Verevon desktop shell, keep realtime state in a worker/utility process with a direct renderer port to avoid IPC hops through the main process.

name: Typed coordinator RPC contracts with capabilities and failure codes
what: The coordinator, main process and renderer exchange only schema-validated calls; an unknown or malformed call gets a precise refusal instead of undefined behaviour.
how: A small contract helper defines services (coordinator-control, coordinator-main, desktop-mount) with methods (zod-style args), events, capabilities and failureCodes. coordinator-control has about 25 methods (gateway connection resolution, box intent, daemon credential mint and spawn, WebAuthn consent, cookie approval, reachability and crash reports); coordinator-main has about 30 (attachments, host settings, secrets, MCP, agent list, transcript tail, voice nudge). Frames are rejected with malformed-frame, unknown-method, invalid-args, cancelled, gateway-malformed-reply, gateway-command-failed, gateway-unreachable or gateway-transport-failed.
verevonRelevance: Same contract style (methods, events, capabilities, failure codes) suits Verevon BFF to worker boundaries.
notes: Quality calibrated to 3: solid but a feature peers commonly ship.

name: Local replica of roster, transcripts, drafts and layout
what: On launch the app shows the last known bots, sidebar sections, selected bot, drafts and layout immediately, then reconciles with the server.
how: Named local stores: roster.last-roster, roster.agent-avatars, selection.last-agent, sidebar.last-sections, transcript.replicas, composer-drafts, send-journal, ui-layout, ui-agent-refs, cloud-agents.infos, client-meta.account-slot, bot-templates.deleted-shares, usage-warning.dismissal, weekly-usage.cache. The main process offers a synchronous boot snapshot (sand:boot-snapshot-sync) and a boot gate with renderer-alive, landed and opened events; durable files are opened with an owner, parse and write error classes and no-follow roots.
verevonRelevance: Offline-first first paint is absent in Verevon (no offline store); a small keyed replica list is a cheap start.
notes: Storage backend is files plus localStorage; no IndexedDB (scout). Quality calibrated to 3: solid but a feature peers commonly ship.

name: Reliability primitives library (deadlines, retries with jitter, stall watchdogs, heartbeats, bounded reporters)
what: Every network and process loop uses the same small set of named, bounded policies, so failures are retried predictably and telemetry cannot grow without limit.
how: Policy factories with kebab-case names: deadline (tc), retry (tf) with initial delay, backoff factor, max delay, jitter none/equal/full and delay hints replace/minimum, stall watchdog (z5) with kick/dispose, interval loop with leading option and tick-failure reporting, keep-alive handle, invariant violation reporter, and a bounded reporter (capacity N, overflow drop-newest) used to rate-limit error events. Process-level uncaughtException and unhandledRejection handlers keep the daemon alive and report scope and kind. A grep of name:"..." policy instances finds about 78 named policies in main-app, 30 in the coordinator, 12 in the daemon and 5 in main-core (for example sand-experiments-bootstrap, gateway-sse-stall, local-exec-sse-reconnect, sand-renderer-recovery, mcp-tools-discovery), so almost every wait, retry and debounce in the client is a named, traceable object.
verevonRelevance: Adopt the same named-policy approach in Model Plane runners so every timer is declared, bounded and observable.
notes: The workspace package is called dune-reliability (package.json).

name: Daemon supervision: discovery record, adopt or replace, respawn limits
what: The local daemon keeps running across app restarts and sleeps; the app adopts a healthy one, replaces a wrong or dead one, and gives up visibly after repeated failures.
how: The daemon publishes a discovery record (pid, startedAt, servingAt, inflightCount, filesKeyId, generation, rejectedAccountScopes, proxyFingerprint) plus connection, credential, supervisor, update-lease and backend-return files. The coordinator supervisor classifies serving, stopped, stale-busy or unjudged (grace after clock jumps), adopts a live daemon with a matching files key, terminates and respawns on key or generation mismatch, and stops after a respawn or files-key-replace limit with a reported reason. Account retire markers and an account generation file coordinate sign-out. Process identity is confirmed by command line (reading /proc cmdline, ps, or PowerShell Get-CimInstance Win32_Process on Windows) so a reused pid is never mistaken for the daemon; the daemon runs as its own OS process started with the app executable and the daemon bundle, with output appended to a log file.
verevonRelevance: A pattern for any long-lived local agent runner: liveness by discovery record, adoption instead of restart, explicit give-up reasons.
notes: The update lease file name suggests updates wait for in-flight work (INF, low).

name: Gateway reachability and DNS diagnostics taxonomy
what: When the Box cannot be reached the app tells apart a user network problem, a DNS problem, a platform outage and a sleeping computer, and reports the class.
how: Gateway kinds loopback, pod_proxy, unknown; clusters (dev, prod labels); DNS outcomes resolved, not_found, temporary_failure, timeout, error; diagnosis classes system_path_failure, independent_path_failure, endpoint_failure, cursorvm_failure, general_dns_failure, resolved_before_probe, inconclusive; coordinator reports reportGatewayReachability, reportBackendReachability (down/back) and reportGatewayDnsDiagnostic. Network return and backend return events cut the reconnect backoff.
verevonRelevance: Cheap, high-value support tooling: classify "agent PC unreachable" causes before escalating.

name: End-to-end trace propagation from composer keystroke to gateway command
what: Latency of a message from key press to Box acceptance can be traced across renderer, coordinator, main and gateway.
how: Messages carry a W3C traceparent plus enter_epoch_ms and composed_at_ms; coordinator-control exposes getRpcTraceWindowTraceparent, reportTransportStage (stage, attempt, traceparent, durations) and reportGatewayCommandSpan (method, rootTraceparent, spanId); spans are exported as OTLP trace requests; dynamic config sand_rpc_tracing {enabled, sample_ratio} controls sampling.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already uses signed decisions; adding traceparent through BFF, Session Core and runners gives per-turn latency visibility.

name: Object storage protocol with presigned multipart and fenced manifest commits
what: Box state and agent files move through object storage with resumable multipart uploads and safe concurrent commits.
how: Enums for multipart failures (PRECONDITION_FAILED, UPLOAD_NOT_FOUND, INVALID_PARTS, CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, TRANSIENT, INTERNAL, RESTART_REQUIRED) and manifest commit status (COMMITTED, RETRY, FENCED); CommitSandBoxStoreManifest takes a manifest and base_etag; admin snapshot and restore of the store.
verevonRelevance: Fencing tokens plus etag-based manifest commits are the right primitive for snapshotting a Space workspace from concurrent runs.
notes: Server semantics not visible; names only.

name: Agent store sync engine for files between desktop mounts and the cloud
what: Files the bot works on stay in sync between the user machine and the bot's storage, resume after sleep, and survive flaky networks and large files.
how: A client sync engine configured by agent_store_sync_client_config (server-driven with defaults): debounce 5 s, idle and passive polling (index poll 2 s, project store poll 4 s), exponential backoff 5 s to 60 s, short-lived store tokens with refresh buffer, jitter, negative caches and a mint circuit breaker (open after 5 failures in 30 s), RPC retry 3 attempts from 250 ms, timeouts (rpc 60 s, blob idle 60 s, round 5 min), lock-release failure thresholds, resume detection by monotonic clock gap (2 min), concurrency caps (s3 8, list 4, hash 4, presign 4), multipart threshold 64 MiB with 16 MiB parts, conflict renames, write barrier and tombstone refresh and pruning. Server primitives: versioned entries with etag, file locks with TTL and holder, tombstones, share and mint token calls.
verevonRelevance: If Verevon gives agents durable workspaces, this is the most complete reference for hydrate/snapshot sync tuning (replaces "inline runs lose their edits").
notes: Quality 5: production-hardened knobs (circuit breaker, monotonic resume detection, fenced roots).

name: Server-driven runtime tuning: about 260 typed dynamic configs with client fallbacks
what: Timeouts, retry policies, concurrency limits and rollouts can be changed centrally without shipping a new client, and the client keeps working with safe defaults if the server is unreachable.
how: A registry maps each config name to a zod schema and a client fallback object; values come from Statsig dynamic configs and gates, with env overrides for QA (SAND_FEATURE_GATE_OVERRIDES, SAND_DYNAMIC_CONFIG_OVERRIDES). Examples with runtime effect: grok_bot_loop_detection mode off, shadow or on; tools_concurrency_config per-tool ttl and maxConcurrent; local_subagent_limits maxRunning 32; nal_stall_detector_timeout_config advisory 20 s and fail 30 s; retry_interceptor_config retriable codes Unavailable, Internal, DeadlineExceeded; http2_ping_config and pool sizes; sand_min_client_version with per-feature minimum versions.
verevonRelevance: Verevon needs a typed, fallback-safe remote config layer for runner policies (retry, concurrency, shadow rollouts) with a shadow mode before enforcement.
notes: Counts: 260 names matched by the fallbackValues pattern; many are marketing or onboarding experiments.

name: Stream stall, hang and retry handling for model streams
what: If a model stream goes quiet the app warns first, then fails, retries on safe error codes and paces text so the UI does not stutter.
how: nal_stall_detector_timeout_config {advisoryTimeoutMs 20 s, failTimeoutMs 30 s}; sand_stream_deadline_config {firstTokenDeadlineMs, idleDeadlineMs}; composer_hang_detection_config thresholds from 2 s to 32 s; retry_interceptor_config retries Unavailable, Internal and DeadlineExceeded with optional maxRetries and delays; text_delta_pacing_config {targetCharsPerFrame, maxLagFrames, barrierMaxWaitMs}; ws_dark_durability_probe_config for websocket idle echo probes.
verevonRelevance: Advisory-then-fail stall detection with UI hints is a small change to SSE run streaming in the Verevon gateway.
notes: Quality calibrated to 3: solid but a feature peers commonly ship.

name: Large request context moved by blob reference with a staged migration
what: Big contexts (files, images) travel as references instead of inline bytes, switched on gradually to avoid breaking older clients.

name: HTTP/2, HTTP/1 keep-alive and websocket pool tuning
what: Connection behaviour (pings, idle timeout, pool size) is tunable remotely to cope with proxies and flaky links.

name: Native sandbox helper with declarative policy (readonly, readwrite, none)
what: Shell commands run by the agent can be confined to the workspace (read-only or read-write) with controlled network access, or run unconfined when the user allows.
how: A native helper binary is started as helper --policy <base64 JSON> -- command with CURSOR_SANDBOX=native in the environment. The policy has type (insecure_none, workspace_readonly, workspace_readwrite), cwd, readBoundary (SYSTEM or WORKSPACE), hardcoded and additional read paths, additionalReadonlyPaths (a write-protection map that also protects git metadata on Linux), additionalReadwritePaths, a scoped temp directory, ignoreMapping (cursorignore and gitignore style), networkAccess or a versioned networkPolicy (default ALLOW or DENY, deny and allow lists, logging, strict flag), allowlist_escalated, enable_shared_build_cache, capture_denies and debug_output_dir. If the helper is missing the call fails with SandboxUnsupportedError and a hint to use insecure_none.
verevonRelevance: A policy-as-JSON contract between agent runner and an OS sandbox helper is the right interface for Verevon sandbox-manager leases (today credential-free and network-less only).
notes: The helper binary itself is not shipped in dist, so enforcement was not verified.

name: Sandbox default read allowlist (observed through REA endpoint extraction)
what: Even in a confined shell the agent can still read the system files tools need (certificates, resolver config, shell rc files, git config, toolchains).
how: REA lists 244 route-like path literals in the daemon, which are the hardcoded read paths: /bin, /usr, /lib, /etc/ssl and pki certs, /etc/resolv.conf, /etc/hosts, /etc/gitconfig, ~/.bashrc and zsh rc files, ~/.gitconfig, ~/.ssh/known_hosts, mise and dotslash caches, /nix/store, /usr/local/go, macOS system and Xcode command line tools paths, plus the bundled ripgrep. Paths are normalised from ~ and glob suffixes and merged with workspace paths when readBoundary is WORKSPACE.

name: Sandbox platform support matrix (macOS yes, Linux preflight, Windows none)
what: Filesystem sandboxing works on macOS and on Linux kernels with the needed features; on Windows the helper only provides a network proxy, so confined shell policies are reported unsupported.
how: isSandboxHelperSupported checks the binary, returns false with a reason on win32 ("proxy-only, no filesystem sandbox"), true on darwin, and on Linux runs the helper with --preflight-only -- /bin/true (15 s timeout); exit code 2 means unsupported kernel features. The reason string is cached and surfaced in errors.
verevonRelevance: A Windows desktop agent must not rely on OS-level filesystem confinement; plan VM or container isolation (Box or sandbox lease) for Windows users.
notes: Important caveat for Verevon on Windows endpoints.

name: Linux workload cgroup attach and OOM score reset for spawned processes
what: On the Linux Box every spawned tool process is placed in the workload cgroup so resource limits apply and the agent cannot starve the host agent process.
how: When CURSOR_WORKLOAD_CGROUP names a writable /sys/fs/cgroup path, a spawn wrapper runs /bin/sh -c with a prefix that writes the shell pid to cgroup.procs and sets oom_score_adj to 0 before exec; paths are validated against a strict pattern; a hop-cwd variant handles long working directories.
verevonRelevance: Applies to Verevon sandbox pods: attach every agent process to a workload cgroup and neutralise inherited OOM scores.

name: Local-exec root confinement with symlink-escape checks and size caps
what: File reads, writes and uploads from the cloud are limited to one root folder on the user machine; symlinks cannot escape it and very large files are refused with a hint to read slices.
how: Root comes from SAND_LOCAL_EXEC_ROOT or SAND_AGENT_PROJECT_DIR, else the home directory. LE resolves a path, refuses anything outside the root, then realpaths both and refuses a symlink that resolves outside; read, write, upload and download reject files over 100 MiB with a message to use offset and limit or a shell command; atomic writes use temp files with O_NOFOLLOW and /proc/self/fd directory handles on Linux.
verevonRelevance: Baseline path policy for any Verevon local-file tool.
notes: Quality calibrated to 3: solid but a feature peers commonly ship.

name: Shell command AST analysis and allowlist prechecks before running
what: Before a command runs it is parsed so that redirects, command substitution and heredocs can be detected and allowlist rules applied to the real executables, not the raw string.

name: Sealed state files for the local daemon (AES-256-GCM with an out-of-band key)
what: The daemon's connection and credential files on disk are ciphertext; the key is handed to the daemon at start so the daemon never touches the OS keychain.
how: Files are written as {sandSealedFile:1, data: base64(iv12 + tag16 + ciphertext)} using AES-256-GCM; the 32-byte key arrives in a typed message {type:"sand-local-exec-file-key", key, computerId}, a key id is the first 16 hex of its SHA-256, and mismatching key ids make the supervisor replace the daemon. how: Tool RequestUserForm and RemapUserFormTargets; coordinator submitUserForm, dismissUserForm, respondToWidget, dismissWidget, submitSecret; vault entries list and upsert (scout RPCs).
