name: Share a bot as a versioned template with export policy
what: Bots can be published as templates (visibility, versions, export policy) and created from a template or share link.
how: Coordinator publishBotTemplate, getBotTemplateVersion, getBotTemplateForSourceAgent, getBotTemplateExportPolicy, deleteBotTemplate, setBotTemplateVisibility, createAgentFromTemplate; tools SearchBotTemplates and CreateBotShareJson; message initiators TEMPLATE_IMPORT and TEMPLATE_SHARE.
verevonRelevance: Agent definitions as shareable versioned templates would speed Space agent creation.

name: Bots operate inside Slack and Teams as channels, with set-up and status tools
what: A bot can be set up in Slack, react to messages, set a status, delete its own messages and offer to connect; Teams has an installable bot app.
how: Tools SetUpSlack, OfferSlackConnect, ReactToSlackMessage, SetSlackStatus, DeleteOwnSlackMessage, DisconnectChannel, UpdateChannel, CreateChannel; scout RPCs for Slack and Teams install and a Teams logo chunk.
verevonRelevance: External channel presence of the same agent (Channel Plane, docs-only today) can reuse this tool set.
notes: Slack and Teams apps are in the reference set, so Grok Bot lives alongside them.

name: Email inbox per bot
what: A bot can claim its own email address, check availability, send mail, search threads and read attachments.
how: Tools ClaimEmailInbox, CheckEmailInboxAvailability, ListEmailInboxes, SendEmail, SearchEmailThreads, ReadEmailThread, ReadEmailAttachment; RPCs create, list and delete inboxes.
verevonRelevance: Verevon mail-to-task is stubbed; per-agent inboxes are the full version.

name: Skills as first-class tools and discoverable SKILL.md folders
what: Bots can use, propose and update skills; skill folders with SKILL.md are discovered from the user's other agent tools.
how: Tools Skill, UpdateSkill, ProposeSkills, GetPlugin, InstallPlugin; scanner checks skills directories for SKILL.md and commands or prompts directories for .md files (depth limited).
verevonRelevance: Matches the Verevon /skill picker; adds self-proposal of skills by agents.
notes: Quality calibrated to 3: solid but a feature peers commonly ship.

name: Streaming lists backed by safety polls, inactivity timeouts and reconcile passes
what: Lists such as cloud agents update live over a stream, but a slow safety poll and an inactivity timeout guarantee they heal if the stream silently stalls.
how: cloud_agent_list_stream_config {enabled_platforms, safety_poll_interval_ms 60 s, inactivity_timeout_ms 45 s, max_consecutive_failures 5, reconnect backoff 1 s to 60 s, reconcile_delay_ms, list page tokens}; the same stream-plus-poll shape appears in the store sync engine (index poll 2 s, project poll 4 s) and in file watcher storm detection (window 10 s, 2500 events).
verevonRelevance: Use stream plus safety poll for any Space list (threads, members, runs) once a push transport exists.
notes: Quality calibrated to 3: solid but a feature peers commonly ship.

name: Agent browser is a real browser on the Box desktop driven by computer use and secure fill
what: The bot's own browser is an ordinary browser on its Linux desktop that it operates by screenshots and input actions; credentials are filled by dedicated tools so the model never sees them.
how: No DOM-automation library (Playwright or Puppeteer) is bundled in the client; the exec protocol offers computer_use and record_screen against the Box desktop, a BrowserSecureFill tool and credential tools, browser identity via browser_id, cookie import and WebAuthn proxy for sign-in, and a noVNC view for the human. Playwright and browser subagent names appear only as gated IDE configs inherited from the Cursor platform.
verevonRelevance: Contrast with Verevon design: Quarry executes browser actions proposed by the Model (DOM level, grants). Grok Bot uses a pixel-level desktop browser plus secrets tools; combining both (DOM when allowed, pixels as fallback) is the stronger plan.
notes: INF based on absence of automation libraries in the client and the tool set; the X11 desktop executor ships in the daemon bundle but the browser application itself and any in-Box browser tooling do not.

name: Client-assembled request context with per-section completeness and a deadline
what: Before each turn the server asks the user's computer or the Box to assemble the context the agent needs (rules, skills, repo and git info, MCP instructions, notes, hooks, permissions), and can proceed with partial context if a section is slow.
how: Exec kind request_context with args (notes_session_id, workspace_id, read_only_pinned_tree_sha, read_only_plugin_cache_root, use_cached, wait_for_workspace_cache) returns RequestContext fields: rules, non_file_rules, env, repository_info, tools, conversation and shared notes listings, git_repos, project_layouts, mcp_instructions, skill_options and agent_skills, custom_subagents, hooks_config, commit and PR attribution messages, user_permissions_auto_run and more, each family with an *_info_complete flag; the result can be served_from_disk_cache. A merged rules service combines several rule sources plus agent-store skills with change coalescing (1 s). composer_request_context_deadline {deadline_ms, max_stale_age_ms} bounds the wait.
verevonRelevance: Context assembly at the edge with explicit completeness flags and a staleness deadline is the right pattern for Space agents that must see per-room instructions, skills and policies without blocking on slow sources.
notes: Quality 5: partial-context semantics make the agent loop resilient to slow edges.

name: Shell exec carries its own governance fields
what: Every shell request ships with the data needed to govern it: parsed commands, redirects, requested sandbox policy, classifier result, an organization denylist, hook approval needs and a secret scope.
how: ShellArgs fields include command, working_directory, timeout and hard_timeout with timeout_behavior, simple_commands, has_input_redirect, has_output_redirect, parsing_result, requested_sandbox_policy, file_output_threshold_bytes, is_background, skip_approval, classifier_result, smart_mode_approval, hook_approval_requirement, output_notification (pattern watch), admin_command_denylist, conversation_id, request_id and secret_scope_id.
verevonRelevance: Put policy inputs (denylist, sandbox policy, secret scope, classifier result) in the exec request itself so the executor can enforce without extra lookups; fits Control-signed decisions.

name: Attention trays: pending approvals, forms and blocks collected per bot
what: Items that need the user (approval requests, forms, blocked bot, pipeline problems) are collected as trays that can be listed, dismissed or cleared.
how: Coordinator methods getTrays (background), dismissTray and clearTrays (person); tray-like kinds action_required, bot_block, pipeline, agent; widget and form responses (respondToWidget, submitUserForm); getAsyncTasks lists background work.
verevonRelevance: An attention inbox per agent (approvals, forms, blocks) is the missing Space notification surface.
notes: Tray semantics partly inferred from method and enum names (INF, medium).

name: MCP tools materialised as a file tree for lazy discovery, with a virtual authenticate tool
what: Connected MCP servers show up to the agent as folders it can browse and read, instead of every tool schema being pushed into the prompt. A server that still needs sign-in gets a status note and a synthetic authenticate tool so the agent can ask the user to connect it.
how: A writer in the daemon watches an MCP lease and, after a 100 ms debounce, writes projects/<id>/mcps/<server>/ with SERVER_METADATA.json, tools/<tool>.json, resources, prompts, INSTRUCTIONS.md and STATUS.md. Names for a ~staging and a ~prev directory exist (atomic replace inferred), stale staging dirs are removed at start, a canonical sorted-JSON fingerprint skips servers that did not change, state fetches time out after 15 s, targeted refreshes touch only the changed server ids and keep cached data if a client is briefly missing, and two servers whose sanitised names collide are skipped. A virtual tool mcp_auth is added for servers in needsAuth (or for all servers when mcp_always_expose_auth_tool is on) with status text telling the model to call it. The request context carries McpFileSystemOptions {enabled, workspace_project_dir, mcp_descriptors[]} where each McpDescriptor lists server, folder_path, instructions and per-tool definition_path; an alternative McpMetaToolOptions mode (gate meta_mcp_tool, default off; slim descriptors default on) exposes a single meta tool instead. Gauges mcp.filesystem.sync_check.* compare expected and actual servers and tool counts.
verevonRelevance: A Space with many connectors can keep prompts small by exposing tool definitions as retrievable files in the Model Plane sandbox workspace, plus a needs-authentication tool that raises a human consent card.
notes: Inherited from the Cursor agent platform (dynamic context discovery) but unusual among chat-room products. Exact swap procedure for ~staging and ~prev was not traced; whether the Box variant of the writer runs on the Box rather than the user computer was not confirmed.

name: MCP execution venues: backend for URL servers, Box for stdio servers, with stale-while-revalidate discovery
what: Remote (URL) MCP servers are called from the product backend, while locally configured command (stdio) servers are pushed to the bot's own computer and run there. Tool lists are cached for a day but refreshed in the background so chat never waits on discovery.
how: The MCP manager in the main process treats a server as HTTP when its config is absent or has a url, calls it through backendMcpExec (ExecuteSandMcpTool, ListSandMcpTools and ReadSandMcpResource on DashboardService) and, when a box MCP execution port exists, adds stdio servers whose config JSON is pushed with loadServers only when the serialized config changed. Discovery results are cached with a 24 h freshness, a stale copy is served while a refresh runs, discovery has a 120 s deadline, plugin servers whose files are not on the Box yet return an explicit "not installed on the computer yet" status, and first-call success or failure per connector is reported as telemetry. Disabled tools per server are filtered from the list and refused at call time, and per-server custom instructions are appended to results.
evidence: dist/local-exec-daemon/main.cjs:L647@2544068 (server or client placement in server config schema)
verevonRelevance: Decide per MCP server whether it runs in a platform-hosted broker (credentialed, URL servers) or inside the agent sandbox (stdio), and cache tool discovery stale-while-revalidate so a Space message never blocks on connector discovery.
notes: Companion to existing record on per-message MCP configuration and box-resident MCP servers; this one adds the placement split, caching and refusal behaviour.

name: MCP call contract: argument repair, files by hash, typed failures with recovery hints
what: MCP calls carry extra safety and recovery data: arguments are coerced to the tool schema when the model gets types wrong, files can be handed over by path plus hash, and failures say whether to authenticate, retry later or re-read the schema.
how: McpArgs adds smart_mode_approval, skip_approval, server_identifier, symbolic_path_arguments[{path, sha256, size_bytes}] and arguments_repaired; the main process repairs arguments against the cached tool input schema (wlt) when the server did not. McpResult has success, error, rejected, permission_denied, tool_not_found, server_not_found and approved. McpSuccess carries content items, is_error, structured_content and system_reminders; McpError carries needs_auth, http_status, retry_after_ms, not_dialed and a McpRecovery {outcome, fresh_input_schema_json, available_tools[]}. Plugin variables are substituted into configs (CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT and CURSOR_PLUGIN_ROOT forms, plugin data dirs), and the result wrapper has hooks to persist images and spill large text.
verevonRelevance: Give Model Plane tool results a typed error taxonomy (auth needed, rate limited with retry-after, schema drift with fresh schema) so the agent and the Space UI can react without parsing text.
notes: Confidence medium: field semantics for symbolic path arguments and recovery outcomes are inferred from names and the client repair code; the server side that fills them is not in the client.

name: MCP server configuration schema: OAuth client credentials, tool allowlist, TLS bundle, cwd and env file
what: MCP servers are described by a single typed config object that covers both command servers and URL servers, including OAuth client credentials and per-server TLS trust.
how: A zod schema accepts command, args, env, url, headers, cwd, envFile, auth {CLIENT_ID, CLIENT_SECRET?, scopes?}, enabledTools, placement server or client, and tls.caBundle (1 byte to 128 KiB), grouped under mcpServers. OAuth tokens and dynamic client information for MCP servers are kept in an mcp-auth file keyed by server id, loaded once per path, written under an in-process save lock, and an older flat token layout is migrated to the {tokens, clientInfo} layout on read (file not read here; secret-bearing file skipped).
verevonRelevance: A Space MCP cockpit needs the same fields (scoped tool allowlist, per-server CA for enterprise gateways, OAuth client creds held by a broker, never by the agent).
notes: Schema shape matches the common mcp.json convention; value is in the TLS and placement fields.

name: Plugin manifests and marketplaces compatible with Cursor and Claude conventions
what: Plugins bundle commands, agents, skills, rules, hooks and MCP servers, and marketplaces can be read from either a Cursor-style or a Claude-style manifest, so an ecosystem plugin can be reused.
how: Marketplace discovery looks for .cursor-plugin/marketplace.json or .claude-plugin/marketplace.json. A plugin entry has a kebab-case name, displayName, source (a string path, a github owner/repo with optional ref and 40-hex sha, a .git url, or a git-subdir with path), version, author, publisher, homepage, repository, license, keywords, capabilities (currently only canvas), logo, category, tags, strict (default true), components commands, agents, skills, rules, hooks and mcpServers, and a variables JSON-Schema subset that must be an object schema (writeOnly marks secrets). minClientVersions {cursor, sand} accepts semver or never so a plugin can opt out of one client. Placeholders ${CURSOR_PLUGIN_ROOT} and ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} are both expanded.
verevonRelevance: If Verevon adopts plugins or skills for Spaces, accepting the Claude plugin manifest and pinning sources by commit sha gives an instant ecosystem and a clean supply-chain control point.
notes: Complements existing records on skills and marketplace discovery by documenting the manifest schema itself.

name: Rules, skills and custom subagents as scoped files with precedence tiers and fail-closed admin disable
what: Agent behaviour is shaped by markdown files found in several places (built-in, user store, home folders of several AI tools, workspace, plugins). Admin-disabled managed skills are dropped even if the disable list cannot be read.
how: Skill roots are .cursor/skills, .claude/skills, .codex/skills, .grok/skills and .agents/skills (the .claude, .codex and .grok ones flagged third-party and gated by an import setting) plus the built-in .cursor/skills-cursor, at project scope and user scope. A merged service sorts skills into tiers Builtin, UserStore, UserHome, Workspace, Plugin, coalesces change events for 1.5 s, and when the managed-skill disable list cannot be fetched it drops every managed skill for that call (fail closed). Wire messages show the file model: AgentSkill {full_path, content, description, globs, scoped_to, argument_hint, disable_model_invocation, disable_user_invocation, environments, disabled_environments, plugin refs}, CursorRule {frontmatter, is_required, scoped_to, environments, warnings} and CustomSubagent {name, description, tools[], model, prompt, permission_mode, is_background, force_default_model}. Built-in and managed skill sync loops exist (constants of 24 h and 72 h sit beside their loggers; which constant belongs to which loop was not confirmed).
verevonRelevance: Spaces could load instructions, skills and sub-agent definitions from org, Space and user scopes with an explicit precedence order, and an admin kill list that fails closed when the policy service is unreachable.
notes: The tier sort is used when a prompt sort context is present; how ties and name clashes are resolved in the prompt was not traced.

name: Agent home directory: transcripts, notes, terminals, large tool output, plans and subagent state as files
what: Everything the agent may need to remember or re-read lives in a predictable folder as plain files, and a managed ignore block keeps the rest of the config directory out of version control.
how: Under projects/<workspaceId>/ the allowlist covers mcps, agent-transcripts (for citation), terminals, agent-notes (shared scratchpad), agent-tools (large tool output); next to it plugins, skills-cursor, skills, commands, plans, subagents and rules. A function rewrites a CURSOR MANAGED BLOCK in ~/.cursor/.gitignore that ignores everything except those directories. Shell children get AGENT_TRANSCRIPTS pointing at the transcripts folder, and the request-context environment advertises terminals_folder, agent_shared_notes_folder, agent_conversation_notes_folder, agent_transcripts_folder, artifacts_folder and mounted agent stores.
verevonRelevance: The Model Plane sandbox workspace for a Space could expose transcripts, notes, process output and tool results as files so the agent cites history by reading paths, and a human can inspect the same files.
notes: Filesystem-as-context is a Cursor lineage idea; here it extends to chat transcripts and notes, which fits a room product.

name: Large shell output: 1 MiB in-band cap, full output spilled to a file, head and tail with elided count
what: A noisy command does not flood the model. The model sees a bounded head and tail with a count of what was cut and a file path holding the full output.
how: The shell stream yields stdout until 1 MiB then a stdout_trimmed event; when the server sets file_output_threshold_bytes the daemon buffers output and, past the threshold, opens projects/<id>/agent-tools/<uuid>.txt and keeps writing up to about 49 MiB (50 MiB minus a 1 MiB reserve), tracking size and line count. Results carry OutputLocation {file_path, size_bytes, line_count} and ShellSuccess and ShellFailure add output_head, output_tail and elided_chars. A rate limiter (60 s window; streaming is suppressed when output exceeds about 64 KiB per second under pressure or 2 MiB per second without, after at least 256 KiB) replaces further streaming with one notice while the command keeps running, and stderr is trimmed at 1 MiB too. The Read tool treats agent-tools .txt files and terminals/<n>.txt like normal files with line ranges.
verevonRelevance: Process results shown in a Space work tab should link to a stored full log while the agent sees head, tail and an elision count, bounding tokens and cost.
notes: Pattern also exists in coding agents; included because the ShellResult contract carries it natively.

name: Stateful shell over stateless processes: environment, options and cwd snapshot replayed per command
what: Each command runs in a fresh shell, yet the agent experiences one continuing terminal: working directory, exported variables, shell options and aliases carry over between commands of a conversation.
how: Per conversation an executor keeps a state string. After every command a bash, zsh or zsh-light dump script prints cwd, environment, options, aliases and functions between __CURSOR_*_STATE_START__ and END markers, base64-encoded in sections; the next shell evals that snapshot. The command text itself is sent through file descriptor 5 and read with a NUL-delimited builtin, not passed as argv. Proxy, sandbox, askpass, conversation id, request id and agent-store variables are filtered out of the snapshot; ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE is unset by exact name after a bug where one command baked it in. A fallback for a vanished working directory returns a clear stderr line and exit 1. On Windows the daemon looks for Git Bash and converts C:\ paths to /c/ form.
verevonRelevance: If Space agents get a persistent terminal in a sandbox, snapshot-and-replay is a robust way to keep per-process isolation and sandbox policy while still feeling stateful.
notes: Quality 5: careful handling of quoting, secrets exclusion and failure cases. No PowerShell state-dump marker was found, so PowerShell sessions are probably stateless (INF).

name: Sudo prompts routed to a human through an askpass socket
what: When a command needs sudo, the password prompt is brokered to the user instead of hanging or being typed by the model.
how: If askpassConfig {helperPath, socketPath, secret} is supplied, the shell env gets SUDO_ASKPASS, CURSOR_ASKPASS_SOCKET and CURSOR_ASKPASS_SECRET, commands are rewritten so each sudo gets -A (unless already present), and an alias sudo='sudo -A' is defined; these variables are excluded from the saved shell snapshot. The helper and socket provider are not in this client (host-supplied), and the feature is skipped on Windows.
verevonRelevance: Privilege prompts inside an agent sandbox should surface as a human approval card, never as a secret the model handles.
notes: Provider side not visible; marked medium.

name: Pluggable permissions service with typed block reasons and sandbox denial capture
what: Every file, shell and MCP action asks one permissions service, and a refusal always has a named reason that the agent and the UI can show differently.
how: The service interface has shouldBlockRead, shouldBlockWrite, shouldBlockShellCommand (returns a sandbox policy), shouldEnforceShellInvariantBlocks, isShellCommandFullyAllowlisted, shouldBlockMcp, isMcpFullyAllowlisted, isWebFetchFullyAllowlisted, addToAllowList, addToDenyList plus ignore-file and repo-block mappings; the shipped default is a permissive stub that the host overrides. Block reasons are needsApproval, userRejected, cursorIgnore, permissionsConfig, cursorFiles, adminBlock, adminCommandDenylist and unsafeResolution, each mapped to a distinct message and to rejected or permission-denied results. SandboxPolicy can request capture_denies, so after the command the shell executor reads denied sandbox operations and streams them as sandbox_denies events (only meaningful where a native sandbox helper runs; the existing sandbox-support record says Windows has no filesystem sandbox).
verevonRelevance: Define a closed enum of block reasons in the Model Plane tool contract so approvals, admin denials and sandbox denials are distinguishable in the Space timeline and audit.
notes: Complements existing records on the three-state permission model and AST prechecks.

name: Typed tool result unions: every tool has named failure variants the model can reason about
what: Tool results are not strings. Each tool returns success or one of several named failures (rejected, permission denied, not found, busy, no space, timeout, OOM killed, sandbox unsupported), so the model gets a precise cause.
how: ShellResult {success, failure, timeout, rejected, spawn_error, permission_denied}; ShellFailure adds abort_reason and oom_kill {kind, memory_limit_bytes}; ShellStream events include backgrounded, hook_context and sandbox_unsupported; WriteResult {success, permission_denied, no_space, error, rejected}; DeleteResult {success, file_not_found, not_file, permission_denied, file_busy, rejected, error}; ReadResult {success, error, rejected, file_not_found, permission_denied, invalid_file}; LsResult adds timeout; McpResult adds tool_not_found and server_not_found; SubagentAwaitResult {complete, still_running, not_found, error}. Every args message carries tool_call_id.
verevonRelevance: Adopt a typed result envelope per tool in Model Plane so Space tool-call cards can render cause-specific UI (needs approval vs denied by policy vs timed out) and tests can assert causes.
notes: Quality 5: consistent across all tools and traced by tool_call_id.

name: Read tool design: permission precheck, special agent files, image and PDF passthrough, bounded text
what: File reads are guarded and shaped for a model: blocked files ask or refuse, images and PDFs are passed as data, text is read in ranges with a size cap, and terminal logs are cleaned.
how: The executor first asks the permissions service whether the read is blocked, resolving a pending approval if needed, then stats the path and rejects directories and non-files. Terminal and agent-tools files use a dedicated reader that normalises line endings, and agent-tools files that look binary are refused; images go through a prepare-for-model step that returns invalid_file with a reason when undecodable; PDFs and some binaries are returned as raw data; text uses streaming reads with offset and limit, an encoding hint, a truncation flag, and an 8 MiB output cap (also above 8 MiB files are streamed); digest_only returns only a digest. Each sub-step runs under a named timeout (3 s, 7 s for streaming text) inside a trace span.
verevonRelevance: Reading Space files for agents should go through the owner-plane ACL check first, then shape output (ranges, caps, digests) in the sandbox tool rather than in the prompt.
notes: Named per-step timeouts with spans are the notable engineering detail.

name: Screenshot and image normalisation before the model sees pixels
what: Images and screen captures are resized and recompressed to sizes the model handles well and to a hard byte budget, without fully decoding them first.
how: Dimensions are read straight from PNG (IHDR) and JPEG (SOF) headers. The default long-edge limit is 1024 px and the WebP screenshot path allows 1280; two canonical computer-use sizes (1280x800 and 1456x840) are passed through untouched; images are re-encoded as WebP and, if over 1 MiB, shrunk by 20 percent per round down to a floor of 8 px until they fit. A passthrough mode exists for WebP without a codec, and an option preserves WebP dimensions.
verevonRelevance: Quarry or the Model Plane should normalise screenshots to fixed model-friendly sizes and byte budgets centrally, so cost and latency of browser-agent runs stay predictable.

name: Polished screen recording: raw proxy capture plus input-event log rendered into a demo video
what: The bot can record its own desktop while it works and deliver a finished, branded demo video as an artifact rather than a raw capture.
how: record_screen starts ffmpeg x11grab on the Box display (mouse cursor not drawn) at the display refresh rate into a 1080p-wide proxy with every frame a keyframe, while an input-event logger records clicks and keys with timestamps. On save the daemon writes recording-data.json (event timestamps relative to the ffmpeg start, resolution, proxies), runs a native polished renderer to produce an mp4 with a brand tag, probes duration, size and frame rate with ffprobe, validates save_as_filename (no slashes, sanitised, .mp4, unique name) and moves the file into the artifacts folder with a cross-device copy fallback. Staging lives in /opt/cursor/recording-staging, ffmpeg must report a frame within 5 s, and prior recordings are cancelled when a new one starts.
verevonRelevance: For agents with their own PC, a shareable replay (video plus event log) is a strong trust and audit artifact for Space members who were not watching live.
notes: Complements the record_screen args record. The renderer is a native binding bundled with the daemon; its look was not inspected.

name: Environment manifest sent with every turn (OS, shell, time zone, folders, sandbox and tool flags)
what: The agent is told, on each turn, exactly what machine and permissions it has so it does not guess.
how: RequestContextEnv includes os_version, workspace_paths, shell, time_zone, project_folder, terminals_folder, notes and transcripts folders, artifacts_folder, sandbox_enabled, sandbox_supported, sandbox network allowlist and whether defaults apply, secret_redaction_enabled, computer_use_supported, is_working_dir_home_dir, process_working_directory, smart_mode_classifier_auto_mode_enabled and mounted_agent_stores {path, kind, alias, read_only, inherited_from_path}. Surrounding RequestContext fields include rules, skills, custom subagents, hooks config, git repos with status, project layouts, MCP options, web search and fetch enabled flags, read_lints_enabled, commit and PR attribution messages, and precomputed human changes.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane runs in a Space should receive a capability manifest (what the sandbox can do, what is mounted read-only, which tools are enabled) that is also shown to humans in the room.
notes: Extends the existing request-context record with the concrete environment fields. Human-change diffs and git info are wire contracts; the producer code was not traced.

name: Agent entity and an admin-readable full agent definition
what: An agent is a rich record (identity, harness, visibility, members, voice, drafting switch), and operators can read a complete "definition" of one agent that lists everything that makes it up.
how: GrokBotAgent has id, legacy_agent_id, name, description, title, avatar shape, colour, version and url, harness, role, visibility, team_id, viewer_is_owner, viewer_session_id, kind, member_agent_ids, people, published_at, team_default_for_viewer, voice id, speed and language, viewer_can_manage and drafting_disabled. AdminGetGrokBotAgentDefinition {agent_ref, identity_only} returns identity (incl. auth id, deletion time and Slack link state), and a definition made of sessions, room members and rooms joined, template imports (template, version, share id), memory shards {scope, scope_key, version, box_backfilled, folder}, routines, recipe skills, MCP settings and MCP servers, or a typed refusal.
verevonRelevance: A portable, versionable agent definition (identity, skills, memory shards, MCP settings, routines) is the right unit for Space agent export, audit and cross-Space reuse, with Control owning authority and Application owning the name.
notes: Wire messages only; purpose (support view or migration tool) is inferred from the Admin prefix and the Box-to-server harness migration records.

name: Memory model: facts, scoped memory shards, team context summary and a rolling summary object
what: Memory is stored as small facts and as versioned shards per scope, a team-level summary is generated from learned facts, and long conversations carry a summary object with an explicit truncation boundary.
how: GrokBotMemoryFact {fact_id, text, learned_at_ms}; GrokBotAgentDefinitionMemoryShard {scope, scope_key, version, box_backfilled, folder}; GrokBotTeamContextSummary {memory_version, generated_at_ms, prose, summary_model} returned with stale flag, skills, learned entries and memory_count; ListGrokBotUserBotMemories and PromoteGrokBotMemoriesToTeam move per-user memories to team scope. ConversationSummary {summary, truncation_last_bubble_id_inclusive, client_should_start_sending_from_inclusive_bubble_id, previous_conversation_summary_bubble_id, includes_tool_results, strategy} lets the server tell the client where history was cut. The tools UpdateMemory, RecallMemory and SortMemories operate on it.
verevonRelevance: Verevon lacks a Space memory scope; a facts-plus-shards model with explicit promotion (person to team) and a generated team summary maps to a Space scope owned by the Model or Data plane.
notes: Wire contract only; the memory algorithms run server side. Complements the existing memory tools record.

name: Agent todo list with dependency edges surfaced to the UI
what: The agent keeps a todo list whose items can depend on each other, and the app can show it next to the conversation.
how: TodoItem {id, content, status PENDING|IN_PROGRESS|COMPLETED|CANCELLED, created_at, updated_at, dependencies[]} is part of the agent protocol; ListGrokBotAgentTodos {agent_id} returns todos[] to the client, separately from the user-facing task list (ListGrokBotAgentTasks, GrokBotTask with state, note and done time).
verevonRelevance: A Space work tab can show the agent plan as dependency-aware todos, distinct from tasks that humans own.
notes: Which tool writes the todos is not visible in the client (server side).

name: Async resource state machine with stale-while-revalidate and write-supersedes-read guards
what: Every cached server resource in the app has the same explicit states (loading, ready, failed with previous value, empty, unavailable), so the UI never shows a blank or lying state, and an old read can never overwrite a newer write.
how: An in-house store framework (package name dune; a devtools hook global is registered) builds resource machines with states loading, ready, failed {previous?}, empty and unavailable {reason}. A version counter makes every write supersede in-flight reads and every settled read check its token, quiet revalidation keeps the old value while a refresh runs (freshMs), a failure policy decides whether to retain the last value, and ClassifiedFailure errors carry codes that can map to unavailable. Settle and ingest commits can be batched at microtask boundaries.
verevonRelevance: Verevon v3 (SolidJS) could adopt the same five-state resource contract for Space lists, presence and run status, with supersede tokens for optimistic writes.
notes: Pattern is well known (SWR, TanStack Query) but here it is a uniform contract across the main process; the renderer uses TanStack Query.

name: Experiments bootstrapped through the product backend, disk-cached, with session-latched gates
what: Feature flags and experiments are delivered by the product backend, never by calling the flag vendor directly, are cached on disk for instant startup, and some gates are frozen for the whole session to avoid UI flips.
how: The client calls AnalyticsService/BootstrapStatsig (with an x-ghost-mode header, an anonymous bootstrap first and an authenticated one after sign-in carrying team id) and feeds the returned config to a Statsig client in bootstrap-only mode (an initialisation check fails the call if bootstrap data was rejected). The config is cached atomically in sand-statsig-bootstrap.json, a poll refreshes every 5 minutes in production (30 s in dev builds) with +0-30 percent jitter, rate-limit Retry-After is honoured, a 30 s bootstrap deadline applies, and developer overrides for gates and experiments are stored in a local override store. 84 renderer-visible gates are listed (for example grok_bot_group_chats, sand_voice_call, sand_box_egress_tunnel, grok_bot_vault, sand_tool_allowlist, grok_bot_agent_mail), eight registry entries are marked as needing an authenticated bootstrap, and a short separate list (currently one gate) is latched for the whole session.
verevonRelevance: Serving flags through the platform (not a vendor SDK in the client) fits Verevon's ZDR and plane rules, and session-latched gates avoid mid-session UI changes in a live room.
notes: A Statsig client key literal exists in the bundle; deliberately not recorded. Extends the existing record on about 260 dynamic configs.

name: Analytics pipeline with a deferred, capped buffer until opt-in is known
what: Product analytics never leave the device before the consent state is resolved; early events wait in a small capped buffer and are dropped if the user opted out.
how: The analytics service starts in a disabled state when the environment says opted out, otherwise in a deferred state with an in-memory buffer capped at 256 events; activate() flips to live, replays the buffered events into a batching client (TrackEvents), and any failure to enable disables analytics. The live buffer flushes by size and by timer, defers when no access token is available or the token check times out, drops the oldest events beyond the limit after a failed flush, and tags every event with client sand, version, flavor, os, arch, host_in_box and a hashed egress IP when known. A once-per-day active event is keyed by reason. Debug logging is opt-in by environment.
verevonRelevance: Consent-gated buffering with a hard cap is a simple way to meet ZDR and privacy rules for client telemetry in Verevon v3.
notes: Complements the existing privacy mode record (x-ghost-mode, opt-out env flags).

name: Crash reporting and in-app feedback correlated by Sentry event ids
what: Crashes are reported with the process and phase that failed, and when a user sends feedback the app attaches the recent crash report ids so support can find the cause.
how: Sentry is initialised in the main process with tags sand.process (desktop-main and coordinator seen in main-core; the daemon and renderer bundle their own Sentry code), sand.crash_kind and sand.startup_phase; invariant violations are reported as a distinct telemetry report type; a helper picks an environment name by build track (sand, sand-lab, sand-nightly, sand-dogfood). The feedback sender POSTs /sand/feedback with message, submissionId, clientSurface, app version, platform, OS version, conversationId, optional wantsResponse or voice-call details and up to 5 sentryEventIds, and maps HTTP 400, 402, 403, 429 and others to the typed codes invalid-feedback, subscription-required, access-denied, rate-limited and unavailable. A bot tool SendFeedback lets the agent file feedback too.
verevonRelevance: A Space feedback action that links the report to trace ids and run ids (and a ZDR-safe redaction pass) would shorten support loops.
notes: The Sentry DSN present in the bundle is deliberately not recorded.

name: Browser-based device login with challenge and polling, and a dev-login guard
what: Sign-in happens in the user's browser, and the desktop app picks up the result by polling with a secret verifier. A developer shortcut exists but refuses to run against non-development backends.
how: The app generates a 32-byte verifier and its SHA-256 challenge plus a UUID, opens /loginDeepControl with challenge, uuid, mode login, redirectTarget sand and supportsSelectedTeamLogin, then polls /auth/poll?uuid&verifier with 1 s backoff growing by 1.2x to 10 s for up to 150 attempts (404 means not ready; three consecutive non-404 failures give up and report a reason class). A 403 with a specific error code raises a denial error. An API key can be exchanged for access and refresh tokens at /auth/exchange_user_api_key. A dev flow targets localhost and a dev-login URL builder builds /auth/cursor_dev_session_token with plan and trial parameters but throws unless the backend host is a development host.
verevonRelevance: If Verevon ships a desktop agent host, a PKCE-style device login that polls the Control Plane keeps tokens out of URLs; the dev guard pattern is a cheap safety rail for test tenants.
notes: Token storage is covered by the existing secrets-at-rest record; no token values were read.

name: Seven-service Connect RPC surface for the agent platform (about 480 methods)
what: All client-to-backend traffic for the bot product goes through seven typed services, which is a useful map of the backend a rival would need.
how: aiserver.v1 services found in the generated descriptors: GrokBotService (309 methods: Box lifecycle and admin, transcripts and watch stream, agent CRUD and access, secrets and vault, email inboxes, plugins, skills, memories, templates and marketplace, messaging, approvals and passkeys, user-computer channel, meetings, rooms, Slack and Teams installs), DashboardService (73: teams, billing and limits, MCP config and execution, canvases, plugin marketplace, machines), SandBoxService (55, largely duplicated inside GrokBotService), AgentStoreService (24: files, locks, tombstones, shares, presigned multipart), AiService (8: models, image generation, tab naming, process metrics, streaming speech-to-text, TTS), AnalyticsService (8) and BackgroundComposerService (7). Counts are 484 entries and 429 distinct names. Only a handful of methods stream (transcript watch, user-computer request watch and open, migration watch, speech-to-text bidirectional).
verevonRelevance: Gives a checklist of control-plane surfaces an agent product needs; Verevon should map each to the owning plane (Control, Model, Application) rather than one mega-service.
notes: Counts come from the generated proto service descriptors (scratch export svc_methods.json). A mega-service with 309 methods is also a cautionary example.

name: Built on the Cursor agent platform: one typed harness reused for a personal-assistant product
what: Grok Bot is not a new agent stack. It reuses a coding-agent harness (exec protocol, hooks, rules, skills, MCP, plugin marketplace, subagents) and adds a cloud computer, presence parking, rooms and a vault around it.
how: Workspace packages are @anysphere/*, protobuf package names are aiserver.v1 and agent.v1, hosts and env names are cursor.sh and CURSOR_*, hook and plugin names mention Cursor and Claude, tools and shims exist for external harnesses (pi, mini-SWE-agent), and the harness-specific folders (.cursor/projects/<id>, ~staging) appear in the daemon. The product-specific additions are the Box, reverse channel, machines registry, routines, Slack and Teams channels, voice, vault and approvals.
verevonRelevance: Confirms that a general typed exec protocol plus hooks, skills and MCP is a stable harness; Verevon can aim for the same contract on the Model Plane (Rust and Go) and add Space-specific authority on top.
notes: Interpretation (platform reuse) is INF on top of SRC names; the homepage field also points at the Cursor site.

name: Per-request environment injection that is unset after each command
what: Secrets and request ids needed by one command are exported for that command only and are removed afterwards, so they do not persist in the long-lived shell session.
how: Child processes get CURSOR_AGENT=1, CURSOR_CONVERSATION_ID, CURSOR_REQUEST_ID and AGENT_TRANSCRIPTS; a request id that contains evaluation-harness markers (cursorbench, sand-eval, eval-harness) is replaced by its SHA-256 so the agent cannot tell it is being benchmarked (INF on purpose). requestScopedEnv entries are accepted only if the name matches [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]* and does not contain CURSOR_SANDBOX; an export-and-unset restore script is generated so the variables are exported for the run and unset afterwards; the state dump excludes these names, request ids and askpass variables. ShellArgs also carries secret_scope_id to select which secret scope applies, and agent-store mount paths passed by environment are added to the sandbox policy as extra read-write paths.
verevonRelevance: Credentials for a Space sandbox command should be brokered per call and never become part of a durable session image.
notes: The secret store that resolves secret_scope_id is server side. Evidence string for the exclusion list is the grep pattern inside the state-dump script.

name: Roster photo cache: content-addressed files served through a token-guarded custom protocol
what: Avatars show instantly and offline from a local cache, but only this app instance can read the cache through its protocol.
how: Cache keys are 32-hex SHA-256 prefixes of avatar url plus version; files live in a cache directory and are served by a protocol handler that parses the request URL, answers 400 for malformed URLs and 403 unless a per-run random token matches (timing-safe compare), 404 when missing, and otherwise fetches via a bound fill function with in-flight de-duplication, a negative cache and bounded retry; the boot snapshot hands the renderer the access descriptor. Only recognised image types under a size cap are accepted.
verevonRelevance: Presence lists in a Space with many agents and people benefit from the same offline-first avatar cache with a token-guarded loader.
notes: Minor; recorded because it shows the app's custom protocol hardening pattern.

name: IPC topology: four contextBridge globals and a few literal channels, the rest over MessagePort
what: The renderer sees only a small, fixed bridge; almost all work flows through one dedicated coordinator channel rather than hundreds of ipcMain handlers.
how: The main preload exposes desktop, coordinatorPort, sandRenderTrace and desktopMount; the VNC preload and webview preload have their own channels (sand:vnc-session, sand:vnc-liveness, sand:browser-passkey-stalled, sand:browser-popup-closed, sand:browser-origin-return), the boot path uses sand:boot-snapshot-sync (sendSync), sand:renderer-alive, sand:renderer-boot-gate-landed and -opened, sand:coordinator-port-request and sand:coordinator-port, and sand:encode-png. REA found 6 context-bridge APIs and 9 IPC operations in the preload directory, of which 7 use dynamic channel expressions that static analysis could not resolve.
evidence: REA analyze_javascript_application(directory dist/electron-preload) ev_89468eaf65e8a177c5ef98147d19d9af3a78dfc96fc59dd90c075e4afb1b193a: 6 context-bridge APIs, 9 IPC operations (7 dynamic channel expressions), 4 renderer listeners; trace_application_feature(api ipcRenderer) no-match on a partial graph (not evidence of absence)
verevonRelevance: A thin, typed bridge plus one capability-checked RPC port keeps the renderer powerless; Verevon's gateway already follows a similar "same-origin BFF" shape.
notes: Complements the MessagePort record; adds the explicit channel inventory and REA counts.

name: Structured client log shipping with bounded buffer and explicit drop accounting
what: The desktop app ships its own structured logs to the backend for support, but never lets logging slow the app, and it reports how many entries it had to drop and why.
how: Log entries (level, message, metadata, timestamp, key) are batched and sent with AnalyticsService/SubmitLogs under a 15 s deadline. A local buffer holds at most 1000 entries; on overflow it evicts selected low-value entries first. Drops are counted by cause (ship_failed, overflow_evicted, replay_expired, backend_dropped, account_rotated) as observed versus acknowledged counters and reported through a sand.telemetry.dropped event; the server receipt {logsProcessed, logsDropped} is checked, and a streak of submit timeouts raises one warning. A separate path ships a sign-in settlement log with the bearer token directly when the keychain is unavailable or the session ends.
verevonRelevance: Client log shipping for Verevon v3 and any desktop agent host should be bounded, ZDR-aware and self-auditing (drops are measured), so support gets honest data.
notes: Shipped log content is already redacted client-side (existing secret-redaction record); server retention not visible.

name: Process supervision: coordinator relaunch with backoff, exit-class telemetry and a renderer crash-loop guard
what: If the background coordinator or the renderer dies, the app restarts it automatically with limits, and only asks the user when it keeps crashing.
how: The coordinator utility process is relaunched by a retry policy (250 ms initial delay, factor 2, cap 10 s, until a signal) and each exit is reported with an exit-code class (clean, breach, bootstrap, signal, other), uptime and a relaunch sequence number; exits under 30 s uptime log at error level. The renderer guard reloads automatically up to 3 times within 60 s after a render-process-gone event, and then shows a reload-or-quit dialog. Startup holds main-window readiness for up to 500 ms for the renderer boot gate. Transport stream drops carry a reconnect id, stream lifetime and whether the window was focused or visible.
verevonRelevance: A desktop or sandbox host for Verevon agents should supervise child processes with bounded restarts and classified exits rather than silent respawn loops.
notes: Complements the daemon supervision record (discovery file, respawn limits).

name: User secrets pushed to the Box through a serialised queue, with counts-only telemetry
what: Secrets the user stored locally are synced to the bot computer one push at a time, and quitting the app stops pushes cleanly. Telemetry records outcomes and counts but never values.
how: A push function exports a snapshot from the user secrets store (OS keychain backed), calls setBoxSecrets, and chains every push after the previous one; stopForQuit sets a flag so later pushes fail with a dedicated error and awaits the queue. Reports contain outcome, trigger, account scope, whether the account is departing, secret count and an error class (keychain_locked, host_unreachable, other).
verevonRelevance: Credential sync to an agent sandbox should be serialised, quit-safe and observable without logging values, matching the Space credential broker plan.
notes: Complements the vault and 1Password records; no secret values read.

name: Client telemetry catalogue shaped around perceived-quality SLOs (114 named events)
what: The app measures what users feel: time to first render, send acknowledgement time, transcript rows that went missing, replica resyncs and event-loop stalls, not only errors.
how: Names found in main-app include sand.render_ttfr, sand.send.ack and sand.send_journal.restore, sand.transcript.parity (shadow-compare of replica and server tail), sand.transcript.tail_row_lost, sand.transcript.window_rows_hidden, sand.transcript.paint_rows_changed, sand.replica.resync, sand.transport.stream_down, sand.box_reachability, sand.box_dns_diagnostic, sand.box_rebuild_escalation, sand.desktop.event_loop, sand.heap.used, sand.vnc_liveness, sand.voice_call_*, sand.update.*, sand.onboarding.*, sand.artifact.*, sand.notification.decision, sand.usage_warning and sand.turn.client_start and client_outcome. 114 distinct sand.* names were counted.
verevonRelevance: Define Space realtime SLOs up front (send-to-ack, first render, lost-row count, resync count) and instrument them in Verevon v3 before scaling the room.
notes: Counts from a grep of quoted sand.* strings in main-app; some names are tag keys, not events.
